title: Sprut CLI exit-code registry
description: Format of registry/exit-codes.json (SPRUT-CLIENT-SPECIFICATION 7.3). The exit code of a command is chosen by `resolution.rules`, in order, first match wins: (1) usage error -> 2; (2) SIGINT -> 130; (3) event stream ended without a final or waiting state -> 1; (4) requested outcome reached (succeeded) -> 0; (5) final (machine of the operation, authoritative state): bootstrap/node_status READY -> 0, bootstrap ACTION_REQUIRED -> 3, bootstrap WAITING_FOR_CONSENT or WAITING_FOR_PRIVILEGE without interactive input -> 4, bootstrap REBOOT_REQUIRED -> 5, bootstrap CANCELLED -> 130, task SUCCEEDED -> 0, task CANCELLED -> 130 (task FAILED falls through to the reason code); (6) otherwise cli_exit_code of the reason code (6/7/8...), fallback 1. A reason code's cli_exit_code alone is therefore not the exit code.

status.description: proposal: may change until fixed at S-1; fixed: changes only with a new major CLI version.

succeeded_final_states.description: Per machine id, the final states with which succeeded=true is consistent (read-only commands such as setup plan may succeed in WAITING_FOR_CONSENT). succeeded=true with any other final state, e.g. FAILED or CANCELLED, is invalid input.

rules.description: Ordered; the first rule whose every match condition holds wins. The last rule must be a catch-all (empty match).

match.description: All listed conditions must hold. Missing boolean inputs count as false.

machine.description: Machine ids (registry/state-machines.json); the input operation kind is mapped to its machine via operation_kinds.

reason_codes.description: Reason codes that map to this exit code explicitly. Must match cli_exit_code in reason-codes.json in both directions.

reason_code_fallback.description: True for the single exit code used by every reason code without a specific mapping.
